prompt: Run the llm-skeleton2grid ablation baseline for as-jpn-tokyo-jr-shape-rect (orig). Decide every cell by reasoning point by point; do not generate coordinates algorithmically.

transcript.note:
Round 1, laid out from scratch. Interchanges first (criterion 1), then whole lines (criterion 2), then a proportional respacing for criterion 3.
1) Frame: I put every degree>=3 point on a monotone column band (by gx) and row band (by gy), so no east/west or north/south relation could invert, then merged adjacent bands only where the merge bought a straight segment. That is why orderFlip is 3 and not larger.
2) Lines made straight: Shinjuku Line runs as one horizontal at rows 25/27 (Shinjuku-Shinjuku-sanchome-Ichigaya, then Kudanshita-Jimbocho-Ogawamachi-*82-Akihabara); Hanzomon runs as one horizontal at row 23 (Otemachi-*83-Mitsukoshimae-Ningyocho); Oedo runs as one horizontal at row 30 (Kasuga-Hongo-sanchome-*94-Naka-okachimachi-*87); Fukutoshin runs as one vertical in column 18 (Ikebukuro-*91-Higashi-shinjuku-Shinjuku-sanchome-*90-Meiji-jingumae); Marunouchi runs as one vertical in column 32 (Ginza-Tokyo-Otemachi-Ogawamachi). The whole west side of the Yamanote loop (Ikebukuro-Takadanobaba-*86-Shinjuku-Yoyogi-*95-Shibuya) is a single vertical in column 15, and its north side (Ikebukuro-Sugamo-Komagome-Nishi-nippori) a single horizontal at row 36.
3) Individual moves for one segment each: Shimbashi to row 17 (levels it with *96), *83 into the Kanda column, *93 into the Roppongi column, Azabu-juban into the Shirokane-takanawa column, *89 into the Tochomae column.
4) Daimon: I first put it a row lower to clear the contracted Yamanote chord, but that inverted the edge winding order at Daimon and Gotanda, so I put it back level with *84. See below - that chord crossing is forced.
5) Criterion 3: instead of one row/column per cluster I spread the bands roughly in proportion to real distance (empty rows in the sparse south, empty columns in the sparse east). This alone took meanDrift from 158 to 49 and cost no hv.
Honest note on cross=2: both crossings are the Mita Line (Shirokane-takanawa-Mita-*84) against the contracted Yamanote chord Gotanda-Daimon. They are not a mistake I can tidy away. Hard rule 0 at Daimon requires Mita to sit south of that chord and *84 north of it, so the segment Mita-*84 must cross it; and putting Shirokane-takanawa south instead only moves the crossings onto Shirokane-takanawa-Azabu-juban and Meguro-Shirokane-takanawa. The baseline scores 0 here only because its own layout breaks the winding order at Daimon, which apply would reject.

transcript.note:
Round 2, two more lines pulled straight, everything else untouched.
1) Namboku Line: I moved Shirokane-takanawa and Azabu-juban into the Roppongi/*93 column, so Shirokane-takanawa-Azabu-juban-Roppongi-*93 is now one vertical instead of two verticals and a diagonal (+1). The merge is between adjacent gx bands with nothing in between, so it costs no order inversion.
2) Yamanote east: I moved Daimon into the Shimbashi/Yurakucho column, making Daimon-Shimbashi vertical and joining it to Shimbashi-Yurakucho, which was already vertical (+1). Mita-*84-Daimon stayed horizontal because the merge only changed columns.
3) That move alone broke the edge winding order at Daimon - pushing Daimon three columns east made Mita look more westward than Gotanda, inverting their order around the station - so I dropped Mita one row into the empty band below it. That restores the order at Daimon, Gotanda, Mita and Shirokane-takanawa (I checked all four), keeps Mita-*84 vertical, and turns Mita-Daimon into a clean 45.
Net: hv 84 -> 86, hvd 108 -> 109, and cross, vtxOn, collide, orderFlip and meanDrift all unchanged. The two crossings are still the forced pair described in round 1.
